task_instance: Given a sample 10-week undergraduate 'Introduction to Machine Learning' syllabus (sample_syllabus.txt), run the syllabus skill's pipeline to produce a supplementary reading list .docx: parse the syllabus into topics/learning outcomes, group topics into sections, search Consensus for 1-3 recent peer-reviewed papers per section, write audience-calibrated summaries and Bloom higher-order discussion questions, and generate the final .docx with the bundled generate_reading_list.js script.
blocker_detail: Phases 1-2 (parse syllabus into course title/topics/learning outcomes, then cluster into 6-12 sections) were completed successfully with local file/text processing (see parsed_sections.json). Phase 3, the skill's core deliverable step, requires searching Consensus (an external academic-search service) via a Consensus MCP connection -- the skill's own Agent Integrity Rules mandate 'Only use what Consensus returns' and explicitly forbid substituting training-knowledge or other-source papers ('Training-knowledge papers labeled [Not from Consensus] and excluded... Section with one paper + note about limited results > section padded with fabrications'). This runtime's granted abilities (file I/O, shell, local dev tools, browser+screenshots) do not include any Consensus MCP tool or equivalent, no such tool appears in this session's tool list, and the task rules explicitly forbid calling any MCP/connector tool and forbid account-bound or paid services (Consensus requires an account). There is no legitimate substitute search source without violating the skill's own integrity rules, so I stopped at Phase 3 rather than fabricate papers or silently swap in a different search engine as if it were Consensus. Because the reading list's content (paper titles, authors, URLs, journals) cannot be produced, the final .docx (Phase 5) was not generated -- generating it with placeholder/fabricated citations would misrepresent the deliverable and is exactly the anti-pattern the skill itself rejects.
